note: Draft curricula pending Tom Harris review. Quiz answers are never published.

programs.name: Build Your Swing — 8 Weeks
programs.description: Fundamentals to full swing in eight weeks, flipped-classroom style: watch the lesson at home, do the homework at the range, check yourself with a short quiz. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Posture and grip
modules.homework: Ten minutes a day in front of a mirror: take your grip and posture, hold five seconds, step away, repeat. No ball this week.

modules.title: Backswing sequence
modules.homework: Slow-motion backswings: ten reps, three times this week, stopping at the top to check the order — club, arms, shoulders, hips.

modules.title: Pelvis movement
modules.homework: Hip-turn drills without a club: five minutes daily. Then ten half-swings feeling the pelvis start the downswing.

modules.title: Strike: low point control
modules.homework: Range session: 30 balls with a towel one grip-length behind the ball. Miss the towel, strike the ball first.

modules.title: Chipping and pitching
modules.homework: Twenty minutes at the short-game area, twice: land three balls in a row on a towel from 10, then 15, then 20 yards.

modules.title: Wedge distances
modules.homework: Build your clock: hit ten balls each at half, three-quarter and full wedge swings, write down the carry of each.

modules.title: Putting: speed first
modules.homework: Ladder drill, 15 minutes twice this week: putt to 10, 20, 30 feet, stopping each ball past the last without hitting it.

modules.title: Take it to the course
modules.homework: Play nine holes, photograph the scorecard into the app, and mark one hole to review with your pro.

programs.name: Score Better — 6 Weeks
programs.description: Six weeks aimed purely at lower scores: short game, putting, wedges and course strategy. Flipped classroom — lesson at home, homework at the range, low-stakes quiz to check understanding. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Where your strokes actually go
modules.homework: Log two rounds in the app (photo the scorecards). Note every penalty and every three-putt.

modules.title: Chipping basics that hold up
modules.homework: Three short-game sessions: 20 chips each from good lies, aiming to land on a towel.

modules.title: Kill the three-putt
modules.homework: Ladder drill twice, plus 20 putts from 3 feet daily — make ten in a row before you leave.

modules.title: One wedge distance you own
modules.homework: Pick your favorite wedge. 50 balls at your three-quarter swing; write down your carry number.

modules.title: Course strategy: play the percentages
modules.homework: Play nine holes hitting whatever club keeps you in play off every tee — driver only where the app agrees.

modules.title: Scoring round and review
modules.homework: Play a full round applying weeks 1–5. Photo the card. Compare penalties and putts to week 1.

programs.name: Women's Golf — 6 Weeks
programs.description: Six weeks built for women, whether you're new to the game or coming back to it: fundamentals, short game, realistic club distances benchmarked to women's data (not men's defaults), and the on-course confidence to book the tee time. Flipped classroom — lesson at home, homework at the range, a short quiz to check understanding. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Setup you can trust
modules.homework: Mirror work, ten minutes daily: grip and posture, hold five seconds, reset. Comfort before speed.

modules.title: A swing that fits you
modules.homework: Slow-motion swings, ten reps three times this week. Film one set face-on with the app.

modules.title: Short game, quickly useful
modules.homework: Two 20-minute sessions: land chips on a towel from 10 and 15 yards; finish with ten 3-foot putts in a row.

modules.title: Know your real distances
modules.homework: Range session with the app: ten balls per club, write down your true average carry for each.

modules.title: The course is yours: etiquette & flow
modules.homework: Nine holes at a quiet time (the app suggests one). Goal: pace, positions, and enjoying it — score optional.

modules.title: Your first scoring round
modules.homework: Play nine or eighteen, photograph the scorecard into the app, and pick one thing to work on with your pro.

programs.name: Family Golf — 6 Weeks (Juniors & Parents)
programs.description: Six weeks for kids and the grown-ups who bring them: games first, short holes early, and a family scramble to finish. Homework happens at putting greens, par-3s and pitch-and-putts — no championship tees required. A parent or guardian enrolls and plays along. Runs equally well as a summer-camp or after-school block, one week per session. Flipped classroom: short lesson at home, playful practice out in the world, a quick quiz kids can ace. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Golf is a game: putting games
modules.homework: Twenty minutes at any putting green (or carpet): play "first to five" from 3 feet, then ladder to 10 feet. Let the kid keep score.

modules.title: Chip it, land it
modules.homework: Chipping catch: land chips onto a towel from 5, then 10 paces — parent and junior alternate, closest to the towel wins the hole.

modules.title: The half swing
modules.homework: At the range or a net: 20 half-swings each with a short iron. Game: call your shot — "high or low" — before you hit.

modules.title: Pitch-and-putt night
modules.homework: Play 9 holes at a pitch-and-putt or par-3 course as a team scramble: both hit, play the better ball. Photo the scorecard into the app.

modules.title: Etiquette as a superpower
modules.homework: Nine more short-course holes, this time playing your own balls. Junior is in charge of pace, safety and where to stand.

modules.title: The family cup
modules.homework: Family match at a short course, front nine. Winner names the trophy. Photo the card; the app tracks the rematches.

programs.name: Your First 90 Days of Golf
programs.description: Twelve weeks from "never held a club" to "I play golf now." No prior experience, no equipment needed to start — rentals are fine and week 2 tells you what to borrow. Short lessons at home, low-pressure practice in the world, and by the end: three real outings played, your own scoring history, and a standing game. Flipped classroom with quick quizzes that build confidence, not stress. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Hold a club, hit a ball
modules.homework: One range visit with rented or borrowed clubs: a small bucket, short irons only. Goal is contact, not distance. Ten minutes of grip practice at home first.

modules.title: The half swing is your whole game (for now)
modules.homework: Range visit two: 30 balls, all half swings with an 8- or 9-iron. Count your clean strikes out of every ten.

modules.title: Putting: the equalizer
modules.homework: Twenty minutes on any practice green: ladder drill to 10, 20, 30 feet, then ten 3-footers in a row. Free, no tee time needed.

modules.title: Chipping and your first up-and-down
modules.homework: Short-game area: 20 chips landing on a towel, then play "chip and one putt" — chip, then hole out. Track your best streak.

modules.title: First outing: pitch-and-putt
modules.homework: Play 9 holes at a pitch-and-putt or par-3 course. Rentals are fine. Photograph the scorecard into the app — your history starts today.

modules.title: Reading the card, playing the game
modules.homework: Learn your scorecard: par, handicap holes, tees. Then nine holes again — count only putts and penalties this time.

modules.title: The driver, finally
modules.homework: Range visit: 15 half-swing drivers off a high tee, then 15 smooth full ones. Fairway-finder first; the hero swing can wait.

modules.title: Nine holes on a full course
modules.homework: Book a quiet-time nine (the app suggests when). Play from the forward tees. Photo the card. One goal: finish every hole.

modules.title: Play with strangers (it’s fine)
modules.homework: Join a walk-on pairing, a scramble, or a league night — one round with people you did not arrive with.

modules.title: Your distances, your clubs
modules.homework: Range with the app: measure your real carry with each club you use. Decide what your (rented or owned) starter half-set should be.

modules.title: Strategy: play smart, score better
modules.homework: Nine holes played to the app’s club and target calls: middle of greens, safe sides, take the bogey. Compare the card to week 6.

modules.title: Day 90: you play golf now
modules.homework: Full nine (or eighteen) with someone from week 9, or your household. Photo the card. Book the next game before you leave the parking lot.

programs.name: Putting Intensive — 4 Weeks
programs.description: Four weeks on the green and nothing else: start line, speed, green reading, and holing out under pressure. You take the same 18-putt benchmark test in week 1 and week 4, so your improvement is measured, not guessed. Works on a practice green, a carpet, or a simulator — no course required. Flipped classroom: short lesson at home, focused drills on the green, a quick quiz to lock in the why. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Benchmark and start line
modules.homework: Take the benchmark: 18 putts — six from 3 feet, six from 10, six from 25 — and record makes and total putts in the app. Then the gate drill: ten minutes rolling balls through a gate two putter-heads wide at 6 feet.

modules.title: Speed is everything
modules.homework: Ladder drill both sessions this week: 10, 20, 30 feet, each ball finishing past the last without racing by. Finish with the 3-foot circle game: six putts around one hole, restart on any miss.

modules.title: Reading the green
modules.homework: Read-then-roll: on ten different putts, commit to a read out loud before you stroke it, then note whether the miss was read or speed. Walk the low side; feel slope through your feet.

modules.title: Pressure, then proof
modules.homework: Pressure sets: make ten 3-footers in a row before leaving, twice this week. Then retake the full 18-putt benchmark and log it — compare to week 1 in the app.

programs.name: Practice Like a Golfer — 4 Weeks
programs.description: Four weeks on the skill nobody teaches: practicing. How to structure a range bucket so it changes your game, the putting and wedge drills worth repeating, how to track progress so improvement is visible, and the 20-minute warm-up that readies you for a round. Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: The range bucket, structured
modules.homework: Two range visits with a written 40-ball plan: 10 wedges to a target, 15 mid-irons alternating targets, 10 drivers to a fairway window, 5 pressure balls calling each shot. Every ball has a target.

modules.title: Drills that stick: putting and wedges
modules.homework: Two 20-minute sessions: putting ladder (10/20/30 ft) plus the 6-foot gate drill, then the wedge clock — half, three-quarter and full swings with one wedge, carries written down.

modules.title: Track it or it did not happen
modules.homework: Add numbers to everything this week: strikes-out-of-ten each range visit, putting benchmark in the app, wedge carries updated. Three lines of notes after each session — what worked, what did not, next focus.

modules.title: The pre-round warm-up
modules.homework: Build and rehearse your 20-minute warm-up: 5 minutes stretch and half swings, 8 minutes through the bag short to long, 2 minutes trouble shots, 5 minutes putting ladder. Then play nine using it and log the round.

programs.name: Equipment & Fitting Basics — Single Session
programs.description: One 90-minute workshop on gear without the sales pitch: the half set a beginner actually needs, how to buy used clubs well, choosing a ball, glove and shoes, setting up a bag, and when a professional fitting is worth it (and when it is not yet). Draft curriculum pending Tom Harris review.

modules.title: Gear that fits your game and your budget
modules.homework: Before the session: list what you own and what you think you need. After: price a used half set online, pick one ball model to play for a month, and bring your questions to the group thread.
